Frozen protocol-100 inventory frames pin the source inspector's consumed wire layout. The envelope, request tags, Session, TerminalDescriptor, and nested DTO declarations were compared with source protocol 99 (`9aba989a`) and source protocol 100 (`4e12b7f2`) before capture; those declarations are identical. Capture used the populated test builder after current-main integration, rather than an old executable. The test compares exact bytes and independently decodes the four restricted responses. Fields cover paired continuity, owned listeners, environment/unsets, transcript metadata, recovery lineage, and a Unicode terminal title. The Connect frame includes an expected owner and a nonempty resume cursor.

Protocol 101 requires replacement of older hosts so recovered native identities enter managed panes and shared admission atomically. It preserves this inventory layout. Tests retain the original protocol-100 files and change only the envelope's version scalar and frame length to verify protocols 99, 100, 101, 102, 103, 119, 127, and 128 against the same frozen DTO bytes. The qualified installed protocol-128 source (`c68275e94`) appends only the startup-state request and response; it preserves these consumed tags and payload layouts. Version scalars at 128 and above use multiple postcard bytes.

Protocol 148 adds `Launch::draft_model`, so its chat Session layout differs from these fixtures. The inspector selects the frozen Session DTO for explicitly qualified legacy protocols and the current DTO for 148. Tests separately verify current responses and reject populated legacy frames relabeled as 148, as well as current Session frames relabeled as legacy. Private versions 129 through 147 have no qualified source mapping. Do not regenerate these binary files from current Session serialization.

Protocol 128 is also used by the separate Antigravity provider draft (#2035 at `97c5e65d2288156c9fa3cbb43c0c7dccf550b9a7`). Its Launch, Session, Snapshot, and existing inspection request/response declarations preserve the installed source's consumed layout, but its appended Provider variant is outside this inspector's known enum. Existing-provider values retain their original discriminants; an Antigravity descriptor is rejected. This qualification does not claim complete compatibility with that draft or arbitrary protocol-128 peers.

The retained-owner bootstrap remains exclusive to 119. Read-only history attachment is qualified for 119, the former matched protocol 127, installed protocol 128, and the current protocol. Their Snapshot and transitive chat DTO declarations were compared with source 119 (`3fcce2a7bf7dcca4cb307de544613aedb0388b61`), main 127 (`0d3b95ab8`), and installed 128 (`c68275e94`). The 119 peer fixtures retain an explicit Snapshot field sequence and use the frozen Session DTO; they never label a current Session packet as an old protocol.
